arxiv-1904-04257.title: Where are the Next Higgs Bosons? Preprint: FERMILAB-PUB-19-143-T CP3-Origins-2019-15 DNRF90
arxiv-1904-04257.creator: Christopher T. Hill, Pedro A. N. Machado, Anders E. Thomsen, Jessica Turner
arxiv-1904-04257.description: Abstract Simple symmetry arguments applied to the third generation lead to a prediction: there exist new sequential Higgs doublets with masses of order < ∼ 5 \mathrel{\vbox{\hbox{$<$}\hbox{$\sim$}}}5 TeV, with approximately universal Higgs-Yukawa coupling constants, g ∼ 1 g\sim 1 . This is calibrated by the known Higgs boson mass, the top quark Higgs-Yukawa coupling, and the b b -quark mass.

arxiv-2011-13952.title: Extreme mass-ratio gravitational-wave sources: Mass segregation and post binary tidal-disruption captures 2020 Extreme mass-ratio gravitational-wave sources: Mass segregation and post binary tidal-disruption captures – References
arxiv-2011-13952.creator: Yael Raveh & Hagai B. Perets
arxiv-2011-13952.description: Abstract The gravitational-wave (GW) inspirals of stellar-mass compact objects onto a supermassive black hole (MBH), are some of the most promising GW sources detectable by next-generation space-born GW-detectors. The rates and characteristics of such extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) sources are highly uncertain.

arxiv-2106-11227.title: FauxWard: A Graph Neural Network Approach to Fauxtography Detection Using Social Media Comments
arxiv-2106-11227.creator: Lanyu Shang, Yang Zhang, Daniel Zhang, Dong Wang
arxiv-2106-11227.description: Abstract Online social media has been a popular source for people to consume and share news content. More recently, the spread of misinformation online has caused widespread concerns. In this work, we focus on a critical task of detecting fauxtography on social media where the image and associated text together convey misleading information.

arxiv-2204-06756.title: A note on the effects of magnetic field on holographic fermions with dipole-like coupling
arxiv-2204-06756.creator: Sayan Chakrabarti, Debaprasad Maity, Wadbor Wahlang
arxiv-2204-06756.description: Abstract In this note, we study the effects of non-zero magnetic field on the fermion spectral function coupled with a non-minimal coupling in the background of a dyonic A ​ d ​ S 4 AdS_{4} black hole. The system can be reduced to a non magnetic one with the momentum being quantized into Landau levels n n .

arxiv-2208-04336.title: Testing Lyman ​ α \mathrm{Lyman}\,\alpha emission line reconstruction routines at multiple velocities in one system. Facilities: HST(COS,STIS) astropy ( 2 ) , stistools, scipy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) , numpy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 )
arxiv-2208-04336.creator: David J. Wilson, Allison Youngblood, Odette Toloza, Jeremy J. Drake, Kevin France, Cynthia S. Froning, Boris T. Gänsicke, Seth Redfield, Brian E. Wood
arxiv-2208-04336.description: Abstract The 1215.67 Å H I Lyman ​ α \mathrm{Lyman}\,\alpha emission line dominates the ultraviolet flux of low mass stars, including the majority of known exoplanet hosts. Unfortunately, strong attenuation by the interstellar medium (ISM) obscures the line core at most stars, requiring the intrinsic Lyman ​ α \mathrm{Lyman}\,\alpha flux to be reconstructed based on fits to the line wings.

arxiv-2306-09941.title: Signatures of the black hole quantum atmosphere in nonlocal correlations
arxiv-2306-09941.creator: Adam Z. Kaczmarek, Dominik Szczȩśniak
arxiv-2306-09941.description: Abstract Recently, it was suggested that the Hawking radiation may originate not at the event horizon but in the quantum region outside of it, known as the quantum atmosphere . The present study attempts to explore this argument further by assessing its role in shaping quantum correlations near a black hole.

arxiv-2310-00235.title: Higher genus maxfaces with Enneper end
arxiv-2310-00235.creator: Rivu Bardhan, Indranil Biswas, Pradip Kumar
arxiv-2310-00235.description: Abstract . We have proven the existence of new higher-genus maxfaces with Enneper end. These maxfaces are not the companions of any existing minimal surfaces, and furthermore, the singularity set is located away from the ends. The nature of the singularities is systematically investigated. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 53A35 1.

arxiv-2401-04421.title: Out-of-time-order correlators of Skyrmion as baryon in holographic QCD
arxiv-2401-04421.description: Abstract As the out-of-time-order correlator (OTOC) is a measure of quantum chaos and an important observable in the context of AdS/CFT, we investigate the OTOC of holographic Skyrmion which is described by an analytical quantum mechanical system from the D4/D8 model (as the holographic QCD).

arxiv-2404-12614.title: Design and Modeling of Indirectly-Driven Magnetized Implosions on the NIF
arxiv-2404-12614.creator: D. J. Strozzi, H. Sio, G. B. Zimmerman, J. D. Moody, C. R. Weber, B. Z. Djordjević, C. A. Walsh, B. A. Hammel, B. B. Pollock, A. Povilus, J. P. Chittenden, S. O’Neill
arxiv-2404-12614.description: Abstract The use of magnetic fields to improve the performance of hohlraum-driven implosions on the National Ignition Facility (NIF) is discussed. The focus is on magnetically insulated inertial confinement fusion (ICF), where the primary field effect is to reduce electron-thermal and alpha-particle loss from the compressed hotspot (magnetic pressure is of secondary importance).

arxiv-2412-21073.title: Near-zero-index behavior in indium antimonide revealed by phase-corrected terahertz reflection spectroscopy
arxiv-2412-21073.creator: Kasturie D. Jatkar, Tien-Tien Yeh, Matteo Pancaldi, Stefano Bonetti
arxiv-2412-21073.description: Abstract We developed a phase correction method for broadband terahertz time-domain spectroscopy in reflection geometry, which allows us to obtain quantitative and accurate values for the complex refractive index of materials. The process is analytical, based on the Kramers-Kronig relations, and does not require any computationally intensive algorithms.

arxiv-2501-17608.title: Spinal study of a population model for colonial species with interactions and environmental noise
arxiv-2501-17608.creator: Sylvain Billiard, Charles Medous, Charline Smadi
arxiv-2501-17608.description: Abstract . We introduce and study a stochastic model for the dynamics of colonial species, which reproduce through fission or fragmentation. The fission rate depends on the relative sizes of colonies in the population, and the growth rate of colonies is influenced by intrinsic and environmental stochasticities.

arxiv-2503-22581.creator: \AtlasOrcid

arxiv-2504-01963.title: LLMs Working in Harmony: A Survey on the Technological Aspects of Building Effective LLM-Based Multi Agent Systems
arxiv-2504-01963.creator: RM Aratchige, Dr. WMKS Ilmini
arxiv-2504-01963.description: Abstract This survey investigates foundational technologies essential for developing effective Large Language Model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems. Aiming to answer how best to optimize these systems for collaborative, dynamic environments, we focus on four critical areas: Architecture, Memory, Planning, and Technologies/Frameworks.

arxiv-2508-17753.title: Talking to Robots: A Practical Examination of Speech Foundation Models for HRI Applications
arxiv-2508-17753.creator: Theresa Pekarek Rosin, Julia Gachot, Henri-Leon Kordt, Matthias Kerzel, Stefan Wermter
arxiv-2508-17753.description: Abstract Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems in real-world settings need to handle imperfect audio, often degraded by hardware limitations or environmental noise, while accommodating diverse user groups. In human–robot interaction (HRI), these challenges intersect to create a uniquely challenging recognition environment.

arxiv-2511-10916.title: Knowledge Reasoning Involving Four Types of Syllogisms Thanks: Supported by the National Social Science Fund of China under Grant No.24FZXB068.
arxiv-2511-10916.creator: Long Wei, Liheng Hao
arxiv-2511-10916.description: Abstract . This paper studies the validity and discourse reasoning of non-trivial generalized syllogisms involving the quantifiers in Square{ most } and Square{ all } from the perspective of knowledge reasoning. Firstly, this paper presents knowledge representations for these syllogisms and formally proves the validity of generalized syllogism AMI-1.

arxiv-2511-21404.title: Revealing Fast Ionic Conduction in Solid Electrolytes through Machine Learning Accelerated Raman Calculations
arxiv-2511-21404.creator: Manuel Grumet, Takeru Miyagawa, Olivier Pittet, Paolo Pegolo, Karin S. Thalmann, Waldemar Kaiser, David A. Egger
arxiv-2511-21404.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Manuel Grumet, Takeru Miyagawa, Olivier Pittet, Paolo Pegolo, Karin S. Thalmann, Waldemar Kaiser, David A. Egger. Fast ionic conduction is a defining property of solid electrolytes for all-solid-state batteries. Previous studies have suggested that liquid-like cation motion associated with fast ionic transport can disrupt crystalline symmetry, thereby lifting Raman selection rules. Here, we exploit the resulting low-frequency, diffusive Raman scattering as a spectral signature of fast ionic conduction and develop a machine learning-accelerated computational pipeline to identify promising solid electrolytes based on this feature.

arxiv-2605-21062.title: Neutron star-companion interaction in core collapse supernovae

arxiv-2606-14775.title: Schema-Agnostic Process Trace Construction: From Raw Tables to Execution Behavior
arxiv-2606-14775.creator: Zhi Quan Joel Lim, Kar Way Tan, Hoong Chuin Lau

pmc-11475968.title: Patient-reported experience measures for people living with dementia: A scoping review
pmc-11475968.creator: Madison Chapman, Rachel Milte, Suzanne Dawson, Kate Laver
pmc-11475968.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The prevalence of dementia is increasing globally, with an estimated 139 million people expected to be living with dementia by 2050. Across numerous countries, substandard care for people with dementia is evident, with quality improvement needed. Recently, a focus on patient-reported experience measures (PREMs) has been utilised in healthcare services as a method of evaluating the care experiences provided and determining areas of improvement.

pmc-11590324.title: Barriers and facilitators to using procedural pain treatments in pediatric patients (under 1 year old): protocol for a mixed studies systematic review with a narrative synthesis
pmc-11590324.creator: Chunji Yan, Jiale Hu, Jiamin Kang, Xueyan Xing, Shumin Tu, Fang Zhou
pmc-11590324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe management of procedural pain in pediatric patients under 1 year old is crucial but often inadequately addressed in clinical practice. Despite proven evidence-based interventions like skin-to-skin contact, sweet solutions, and breastfeeding, their implementation remains sporadic.

pmc-11644922.title: HDCTfusion: Hybrid Dual-Branch Network Based on CNN and Transformer for Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
pmc-11644922.creator: Wenqing Wang, Lingzhou Li, Yifei Yang, Han Liu, Runyuan Guo
pmc-11644922.description: The purpose of infrared and visible image fusion is to combine the advantages of both and generate a fused image that contains target information and has rich details and contrast. However, existing fusion algorithms often overlook the importance of incorporating both local and global feature extraction, leading to missing key information in the fused image.

pmc-12609193.title: Deep Learning-Based Inverse Design of Stochastic-Topology Metamaterials for Radar Cross Section Reduction
pmc-12609193.creator: Chao Zhang, Chunrong Zou, Shaojun Guo, Yanwen Zhao, Tongsheng Shen, Andrea Sorrentino
pmc-12609193.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Electromagnetic (EM) metamaterials have a wide range of applications due to their unique properties, but their design is often based on specific topological structures, which come with certain limitations. Designing with stochastic topologies can provide more diverse EM properties. However, this requires experienced designers to search and optimise in a vast design space, which is time-consuming and requires substantial computational resources.

pmc-12638856.title: Impact of statins on short and long term mortality in severe community acquired pneumonia in the intensive care unit
pmc-12638856.creator: Juan Olivella-Gomez, Natalia Sanabria-Herrera, Esteban Garcia-Gallo, Sara Duque, David Luna, Henry Oliveros, Andrew Conway Morris, Alejandro Rodriguez, Djillali Annane, Ignacio Martin-Loeches, Luis Felipe Reyes
pmc-12638856.description: Severe community-acquired pneumonia (sCAP) carries high mortality. While co-adjuvant therapies remain limited, statins have shown potential benefits. This study simulated a randomised controlled trial (RCT) using real-world data to evaluate the effect of statins on mortality in ICU patients with sCAP. A propensity score matching (PSM) analysis was conducted using the MIMIC-IV database.

pmc-12713041.title: Validation of Basque “Test of Adherence to Inhalers” in Asthma and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
pmc-12713041.creator: Daniela Mestre, Miren Orive, María Gascón, Amaia Bilbao-González, Nerea González-Hernández, Sandra Dorado-Arenas, Amaia Aramburu, José M Quintana, On behalf of The Osakidetza-Respiratory translation HRQoL group
pmc-12713041.description: PurposeTo adapt the Test of Adherence to Inhalers (TAI) questionnaire to Basque language and evaluate the psychometric properties.Patients and MethodsA cross-sectional observational study was carried out. We recruited Basque-speaking adults aged ≥18 years who attended the respiratory outpatient clinics in the last 5 years for follow-up with a diagnosis of asthma (n=249) or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (n=149).

pmc-13355271.title: Exploration and experimental validation of oxidative stress-related diagnostic genes in interstitial cystitis based on transcriptomics
pmc-13355271.creator: Daofeng Zhang, Junhao Zheng, Haorui Li, Rongyang Jin, Hao Chen, Xiaoliang Sun, Haiyang Zhang
pmc-13355271.description: BackgroundInterstitial cystitis (IC) is a chronic pain syndrome with an elusive diagnosis and poorly understood pathogenesis, in which oxidative stress (OS) is increasingly implicated. This study aimed to identify and validate OS-related diagnostic biomarkers for IC using an integrative computational and experimental approach.MethodsWe performed bioinformatics analysis on human bladder transcriptomic datasets (GSE11783, GSE57560) to identify OS-related differentially expressed genes (DEOSGs).

pmc-13384109.title: Engineering an Ni9S8@Fe-NiP-O2 core–shell catalyst: high activity and stability for oxygen/hydrogen evolution in alkaline and ammonia-containing media
pmc-13384109.creator: Kangkang Zhao, Haonan Jiang, Yunjie Ke, Meizhen Dai, Hengqi Liu, Shiwei Song, Yucai Li, Depeng Zhao, Rongda Zhao, Lihua Miao
pmc-13384109.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). To address the issues of low activity, inadequate stability, and susceptibility to deactivation in ammonia-containing alkaline water electrolysis catalysts, Ni9S8@Fe-NiP-O2 bifunctional electrocatalysts with a fractional core–shell structure were effectively synthesised using a phosphating oxidation coupling strategy. The Ni9S8@N3Fe-PBA precursor underwent structural transformation to form porous cubic-like particles, exhibiting significant electronic interaction between the Ni9S8 core and the Fe-NiP-O2 shell, which effectively modulated the surface electronic structure.

pmc-13568268.title: Performance of Asphalt Mixtures Hybrid-Modified with Industrial Diatomite By-Products and Different Microfibres
pmc-13568268.creator: Mustafa Taha Aslan, Erol İskender, Cansu İskender, Osman Ünsal Bayrak, Turgay Ömür, Atakan Aksoy
pmc-13568268.description: This study evaluated asphalt mixtures incorporating two diatomite types (D1 and D2) at contents of 10% and 15% by binder weight and three fibre treatments added by aggregate weight: polyacrylonitrile (PAN) (0.065%), polyethylene terephthalate (PET) (0.10%), and basalt fibre (0.30%). An unmodified mixture and a mixture containing 5% styrene–butadiene–styrene (SBS) by binder weight were included as references.

uslaw-usc-t10-s7036.title: 10 U.S.C. § 7036 — Chiefs of branches: appointment; duties
uslaw-usc-t10-s7036.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s7036.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part I (Organization); Chapter 705 (The Army Staff). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) There are in the Army the following officers: (1) Chief of Engineers. (2) Surgeon General. (3) Judge Advocate General. (4) Chief of Chaplains. (b) Each officer named in subsection (a), except the Judge Advocate General, shall be appointed by the President.

uslaw-usc-t22-s8302.title: 22 U.S.C. § 8302 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t22-s8302.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s8302.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 90 (Volunteers For Prosperity Program). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this chapter: (1) VfP Office The term “VfP Office” means the Office of Volunteers for Prosperity of the United States Agency for International Development. (2) VfP Program The term “VfP Program” means the Volunteers for Prosperity Program established through Executive Order.

uslaw-usc-t31-s3112.title: 31 U.S.C. § 3112 — Sinking fund for retiring and cancelling bonds and notes
uslaw-usc-t31-s3112.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t31-s3112.description: United States Code, Title 31 (Money And Finance); Chapter 31 (Public Debt); Subchapter I (Borrowing Authority). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) The Department of the Treasury has a sinking fund for retiring bonds and notes issued under this chapter. Amounts in the fund are appropriated for payment of bonds and notes at maturity or for their redemption or purchase before maturity.

uslaw-usc-t42-s10262.title: 42 U.S.C. § 10262 — Nuclear Waste Technical Review Board
uslaw-usc-t42-s10262.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s10262.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 108 (Nuclear Waste Policy); Subchapter V (Nuclear Waste Technical Review Board). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Establishment There is established a Nuclear Waste Technical Review Board that shall be an independent establishment within the executive branch. (b) Members (1) The Board shall consist of 11 members who shall be appointed.
